HowYouDoin is an unofficial app. It is not made, endorsed or supported by Meta (WhatsApp, Messenger, Instagram), Telegram, Signal or Slack. Most of these services don't officially allow third-party apps, so they could limit or block an account that uses one. HowYouDoin is provided "as is", without warranty; you use it at your own risk.

Your accounts connect straight from this phone. Messages, contacts and login data stay on the phone and go only to the networks themselves; HowYouDoin has no servers of its own in this mode and collects no analytics. If "Back up logins" is on, the logins are also in your phone's Google backup, end-to-end encrypted with your screen lock. Crash reports stay on the phone unless you share them.

WhatsApp, Messenger and Instagram are trademarks of Meta Platforms, Inc.; Telegram of Telegram FZ-LLC; Signal of Signal Technology Foundation; Slack of Slack Technologies, LLC; Matrix of The Matrix.org Foundation. Their logos are shown only to tell which network a chat belongs to (icons from Simple Icons, CC0).
HowYouDoin itself is free software under the GNU Affero General Public License v3. It's built on these open-source projects; tap one to see its website or license.

Choose "pairing code" if WhatsApp is on this phone: WhatsApp → Linked devices → Link a device → Link with phone number instead, and type the code HowYouDoin shows. With WhatsApp on another phone, "QR code" works too.
Log in on the Facebook or Instagram page that opens inside HowYouDoin. For encrypted Messenger chats, enter your Messenger PIN once to bring back their history.
Choose "phone number": Telegram sends a login code to the Telegram app (or by SMS). The QR code option needs a second screen, because Telegram only scans codes with the camera.

HowYouDoin joins your Signal account as a linked device, like Signal Desktop: in Signal open Settings → Linked devices → Link a new device and scan the code. Signal scans with the camera, so the code has to be on a different screen from the phone Signal runs on.
Your chats connect straight from this phone; no server stores them. HowYouDoin keeps the connections open in the background, which is what the "Connected on this device" notification means.
